key_insight: Learned smoothers improve single-pass multigrid accuracy at a fixed smoothing budget, but the tested CPU implementation provides no computational advantage over classical solvers.
engineering_relevance: For high-contrast elliptic finite element problems, better fixed-budget accuracy should not be mistaken for faster practical solution.
method: Train only the smoothers within an operator-adapted multigrid V-cycle.
Use operator-dependent transfers, Galerkin coarse operators, near-kernel deflation and an energy-norm safeguard.
Compare energy errors against classical smoothing at fixed and increased iteration budgets.
evidence_signal: On fresh problems, one learned pass reduced energy error by factors of 5.7–6.1 for conductive channels and 1.38–1.45 for insulating barriers relative to four-step Jacobi-preconditioned CG smoothing; classical accuracy caught up between 8–14 and 5–8 steps per call, respectively.
watch_item: Load changes and floating islands further limit accuracy, and fixed-input Krylov comparisons do not establish superiority over all polynomial-smoothed cycles.
paper_title: Learned smoothing in operator-adapted multigrid: controlled accuracy gains and computational limits
